findings.text: check_a_review_comment_is_not_the_landing is green under the very mutation it claims to guard. Its s2 fixture (PROMOTION fixture, _promotion_comments()) carries c-close-s2 as well as the trailing c-run-<REVIEW_A> comment, so both the shipped rule and the reverted last-comment rule return the close comment and the assertion can never see a review quoted. The declared negative control proves the gap: negative-control-492a890fac.log selects -k 'promotion or reviews_last_comment' and reports '1 failed, 2 passed, 15 deselected' — only the promotion case reddens, and test_a_reviews_last_comment_is_not_the_landing passes while the landing rule is reverted. The case needs a section whose only comments are a landed run's c-run- and a review's trailing c-run-, so the fallback it names is the one that could quote the review.

_run_comment_id re-implements a derivation the repository already performs twice: reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:1452 and :2628 each build the landing comment id as f"{RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX}{re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '-', run_id)}". The addition extends reckon/crew/plan_review.py:252 by importing RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX, but the normalisation rule — the half that has to agree with the writer for the lookup to find anything — is now a third copy, so a change to the writer's rule silences: the reader would stop matching and every promotion-landed section would read as having no landing comment. The owner is reckon/crew/plan_review.py, which holds the prefix constant and _is_run_comment but no builder; extracting run_comment_id there and calling it from all three sites is the cut that removes the copies.
